meta.project_name: Crypto Trend-Break Knowledge Base & Indicator Pipeline
meta.goal: Formalize classical technical-analysis and price-action concepts into codeable rules, features, filters, confirmations, invalidations and heuristics, sufficient to (1) drive a Pine Script v6 trend-break indicator and (2) label a dataset for ML training, without inventing new facts beyond well-established TA concepts.
assumptions: Crypto trades 24/7 with no session gaps, unlike the equities/futures markets most cited sources were originally written for.
Base execution timeframes are 5m and 15m; 1h is used as higher-timeframe (HTF) context only, not as an independent signal source in this scope.
All signals are computed from confirmed, closed bars unless a rule is explicitly marked as an intrabar/heuristic early-warning.
Pivot-based swing detection has an inherent confirmation lag (pivot_right bars) — this is disclosed latency, not repaint.
No proprietary or invented claims are attributed to the listed authors beyond commonly known, widely published core concepts of their respective methods.

knowledge_base.summary: Core technical-analysis literature converges on a small set of reusable primitives: trend is defined by the sequence of swing highs/lows (Murphy, Wyckoff, Beggs/ICT-style structure); reversals are confirmed by a break of that swing sequence (change of character) rather than by a single indicator; candlestick patterns (Nison) and oscillator divergences (Elder) act as confirming/timing signals, not standalone triggers; volume (Wyckoff) validates or invalidates a move; and higher-timeframe context (Murphy, Elder's triple screen) filters which lower-timeframe signals are worth acting on. Bulkowski's geometric chart patterns are statistically documented but not precisely formalizable without a trained classifier, so they are treated as heuristic filters rather than direct rules.

crypto_specific_notes: 24/7 continuous trading means no opening-gap analysis applies; swing/pivot logic must rely purely on intraday price action.
Perpetual futures funding-rate dynamics can produce wicks and short-lived false breakouts not explained by classical equity-market TA — treat wick-only breaks with extra skepticism (heuristic).
Liquidity is fragmented across exchanges; a break confirmed on one venue's feed may not reflect the broader market — data source should be disclosed and consistent.
Low-cap/altcoin pairs have thinner order books, inflating noise and false-breakout rates relative to BTC/ETH — noise-filter parameters (ATR multiples) likely need per-symbol tuning.

Volatility clusters around specific hours/sessions (US/Asia overlap, weekend thinning) more than in traditional markets with fixed sessions — a volatility-regime feature is recommended rather than assuming stationarity.
No circuit breakers or trading halts exist in most crypto venues, so extreme-volatility bars are not filtered by the exchange the way they might be in equities.

rules.rule: Uptrend is defined by a sequence of higher highs and higher lows.
rules.formalization: if last_high_type == 'HH' and last_low_type == 'HL': trend = 'up'

rules.rule: Downtrend is defined by a sequence of lower highs and lower lows.
rules.formalization: if last_high_type == 'LH' and last_low_type == 'LL': trend = 'down'

rules.rule: A change of character occurs when price closes beyond the most recent swing point against the current trend.
rules.formalization: if trend == 'up' and close < last_swing_low: choch_down = true

rules.rule: A break of structure occurs when price closes beyond the most recent swing point in the direction of the current trend, confirming continuation.
rules.formalization: if trend == 'up' and close > last_swing_high: bos_up = true

rules.rule: After a break, price often returns to the broken level before continuing; a held retest strengthens the signal.
rules.formalization: if bars_since(break) <= N and abs(close - level) <= k*ATR and subsequent close moves away from level: retest_hold = true

rules.rule: A false breakout occurs when price pierces a level intrabar (wick) but closes back on the original side within a short window.
rules.formalization: if wick_beyond_level and close_back_inside(within M bars): false_breakout = true

rules.rule: A bullish/bearish engulfing candle's body fully covers the prior candle's opposite-direction body.
rules.formalization: close>open and close[1]<open[1] and close>=open[1] and open<=close[1] and body>=body[1]*ratio

rules.rule: A pin bar / hammer / hanging man has a small body and a long wick at least k times the body on one side.
rules.formalization: wick >= body*k and opposite_wick <= body

rules.rule: Morning/evening star is a three-candle reversal: strong trend candle, small-body indecision candle, strong opposite candle closing beyond the midpoint of the first.
rules.formalization: trend_candle then small_body_candle (body <= range*ratio) then reversal_candle closing past midpoint of candle 1

rules.rule: Pattern strength increases when it occurs at a structural level and/or with above-average volume.
rules.formalization: score += level_proximity_bonus + volume_spike_bonus

rules.rule: Regular bullish divergence: price makes a lower pivot low while the oscillator makes a higher pivot low.
rules.formalization: if price_pivot < prev_price_pivot and osc_value_at_pivot > osc_value_at_prev_pivot: regular_bullish_div = true

rules.rule: Regular bearish divergence: price makes a higher pivot high while the oscillator makes a lower pivot high.
rules.formalization: if price_pivot > prev_price_pivot and osc_value_at_pivot < osc_value_at_prev_pivot: regular_bearish_div = true

rules.rule: Hidden divergence (price/oscillator mismatch in the opposite pattern) suggests trend continuation rather than reversal.
rules.formalization: mirror of regular divergence conditions with price/oscillator roles swapped

rules.rule: Volume above its recent average confirms the significance of a breakout or pattern.
rules.formalization: volume >= SMA(volume, 20) * mult

rules.rule: Climax volume (Wyckoff) — an unusually large volume spike at a price extreme can mark exhaustion and reversal.
rules.formalization: volume >= SMA(volume,20)*mult2 and range >= k*ATR at a local price extreme

rules.rule: Swings smaller than a volatility-scaled minimum size should be discarded as noise before classification.
rules.formalization: if abs(pivot - prev_pivot) < ATR * min_mult: ignore_pivot

rules.rule: Higher-timeframe trend/bias should filter or weight lower-timeframe signals rather than trigger signals on its own.
rules.formalization: htf_bias in {up, down, neutral} used as a scoring weight, not a standalone trigger

rules.rule: Classical geometric reversal patterns (double top/bottom, head and shoulders) are statistically documented but geometrically ambiguous to define precisely.
rules.formalization: not precisely codeable without a trained geometric-pattern classifier

rules.rule: A false breakout of a geometric chart-pattern level (return inside after piercing) weakens the pattern's validity.
rules.formalization: requires arbitrary level definition from the geometric pattern; not precisely codeable

rules.rule: OBV divergence against price can add confirmation but OBV is unbounded, unlike RSI/MACD, making zone-based quality filters unreliable.
rules.formalization: obv_pivot vs price_pivot mismatch, used only as an auxiliary confluence flag

definitions.HH: A confirmed swing high with a value greater than the previous confirmed swing high.
definitions.HL: A confirmed swing low with a value greater than the previous confirmed swing low.
definitions.LH: A confirmed swing high with a value less than the previous confirmed swing high.
definitions.LL: A confirmed swing low with a value less than the previous confirmed swing low.
definitions.break_of_structure: Price closes beyond the most recent swing point in the direction of the prevailing trend, confirming continuation.
definitions.change_of_character: Price closes beyond the most recent swing point against the prevailing trend, signaling a possible reversal (the primary trend_break trigger).
definitions.retest: After a change of character, price returns to within a tolerance band of the broken level and then closes away from it in the direction of the break, strengthening confirmation.
definitions.false_breakout: Price closes back on the original side of a broken level within a short bar window after the break, invalidating it.

swing_detection.method: Confirmed pivot high/low: a bar's high(low) is the maximum(minimum) within a symmetric window of pivot_left bars before and pivot_right bars after it; confirmation is inherently delayed by pivot_right bars, which is disclosed latency, not repaint. A volatility-scaled noise filter discards pivots too close to the prior opposite-type pivot.

parameters.noise_filter: A new pivot is accepted only if abs(new_pivot - last_accepted_opposite_type_pivot) >= ATR(atr_len) * min_swing_distance; min_swing_distance is expressed as a multiple of ATR.

transition_rules: range -> uptrend: first confirmed HH+HL pair forms.
range -> downtrend: first confirmed LH+LL pair forms.
uptrend -> transition: close crosses below the last confirmed swing low (raw change-of-character trigger) while awaiting hold-bar confirmation.
downtrend -> transition: close crosses above the last confirmed swing high (raw change-of-character trigger) while awaiting hold-bar confirmation.
transition -> downtrend: the pending change-of-character survives the configured confirmation window without price closing back through the broken level.
transition -> uptrend: symmetric case for a bullish change-of-character surviving confirmation.
transition -> previous state: price closes back through the broken level before the confirmation window elapses (false-breakout invalidation).
an opposing raw trigger arriving during transition cancels the pending state (treated as evidence against it) and immediately arms a new transition in the opposing direction.

trend_break_rules.trend_break_up: Confirmed when trend_state was 'downtrend' (or 'transition' toward up), price closes above the last confirmed swing high, and the change-of-character survives the configured hold-bar confirmation window (0 bars = immediate).
trend_break_rules.trend_break_down: Confirmed when trend_state was 'uptrend' (or 'transition' toward down), price closes below the last confirmed swing low, and the change-of-character survives the configured hold-bar confirmation window (0 bars = immediate).

pseudo_code: ph = confirmed_pivot_high(high, pivot_left, pivot_right); pl = confirmed_pivot_low(low, pivot_left, pivot_right)
if ph is new and abs(ph - last_swing_high) >= ATR*min_swing_distance: classify HH/LH vs last_swing_high; last_swing_high = ph
if pl is new and abs(pl - last_swing_low) >= ATR*min_swing_distance: classify HL/LL vs last_swing_low; last_swing_low = pl
trend_state updates ONLY through the confirmation pathway below, never directly from HH/HL/LH/LL classification alone
choch_up_raw = trend_state=='downtrend' and close crosses above last_swing_high
choch_down_raw = trend_state=='uptrend' and close crosses below last_swing_low
if hold_bars <= 0: confirm immediately on choch_*_raw
else: enter 'transition', track bars_since_trigger; cancel if price closes back through the level before hold_bars elapse; confirm and update trend_state if it survives
bos_up/bos_down are computed the same way but in the direction of the existing trend_state, and are treated as continuation context, not as a trend_break trigger

patterns.name: bullish_engulfing
conditions: current body fully covers previous body
context_requirements: stronger after a preceding decline or near a swing low
patterns.strength_score_hint: base 2; +1 near structural level; +1 on volume spike

patterns.name: bearish_engulfing
conditions: current body fully covers previous body
context_requirements: stronger after a preceding advance or near a swing high
patterns.strength_score_hint: base 2; +1 near structural level; +1 on volume spike

patterns.name: pin_bar_rejection
context_requirements: direction determined by which side the long wick is on
needs a nearby level to be meaningful, especially on 5m
patterns.strength_score_hint: base 1-2; +1 near structural level; +1 on volume spike

patterns.name: hammer
conditions: pin_bar_rejection shape with lower wick dominant
context_requirements: must occur after a preceding decline (context distinguishes it from a generic bullish pin bar)
patterns.strength_score_hint: base 2; +1 near structural level; +1 on volume spike

patterns.name: hanging_man
conditions: pin_bar_rejection shape with lower wick dominant
context_requirements: must occur after a preceding advance (context distinguishes it from a generic bullish-shaped pin bar)
patterns.strength_score_hint: base 2; +1 near structural level; +1 on volume spike

patterns.name: morning_star
conditions: candle[0] bullish, closing past midpoint of candle[2]
context_requirements: stronger near a swing low or structural support
patterns.strength_score_hint: base 3; +1 near structural level; +1 on volume spike

patterns.name: evening_star
conditions: candle[0] bearish, closing past midpoint of candle[2]
context_requirements: stronger near a swing high or structural resistance
patterns.strength_score_hint: base 3; +1 near structural level; +1 on volume spike

scoring_rules: score -= 1 in strict mode if the pattern direction conflicts with higher-timeframe bias
on 5m, patterns without a volume-spike confirmation should be weighted down or treated as heuristic due to noise
pseudo_code: body = abs(close-open); range_ = high-low; upper_wick = high - max(close,open); lower_wick = min(close,open) - low
bull_engulf = close>open and close[1]<open[1] and close>=open[1] and open<=close[1] and body>=body[1]*min_ratio
pin_bull_shape = lower_wick >= body*k and upper_wick<=body and close>open
hammer = pin_bull_shape and prior_move_down; hanging_man = pin_bear_shape and prior_move_up
morning_star = bearish(candle[2]) and small_body(candle[1]) and bullish(candle[0]) and close > midpoint(open[2],close[2])
score computed via scoring_rules above, then held active for a short confirmation window so it can still contribute when a structure break lands a few bars later

divergence_types.name: regular_bullish
divergence_types.price_condition: new confirmed pivot low lower than the previous confirmed pivot low
divergence_types.oscillator_condition: oscillator value at the new pivot is higher than at the previous pivot
divergence_types.pivot_rules: evaluated at the bar of the confirmed price pivot, using the oscillator's value at that same bar rather than an independently-detected oscillator pivot, for reliability
divergence_types.lookback_rules: gap between compared pivots must fall within [min_bars, max_bars]; price change between pivots must exceed a minimum percentage
quality_filters: RSI and MACD histogram agreement (confluence bonus)
RSI below an oversold-ish zone at the pivot
gap not too close to the minimum bar distance (avoids noisy signals)
divergence_types.strength_score_hint: base 1; +1 confluence; +1 strong price/oscillator change magnitude; +1 RSI extreme zone; -1 if gap near minimum

divergence_types.name: regular_bearish
divergence_types.price_condition: new confirmed pivot high higher than the previous confirmed pivot high
divergence_types.oscillator_condition: oscillator value at the new pivot is lower than at the previous pivot
divergence_types.pivot_rules: same price-pivot-anchored approach as regular_bullish, mirrored
quality_filters: RSI above an overbought-ish zone at the pivot
gap not too close to the minimum bar distance
divergence_types.strength_score_hint: base 1; +1 confluence; +1 strong magnitude; +1 RSI extreme zone; -1 if gap near minimum

divergence_types.name: hidden_bullish
divergence_types.price_condition: new confirmed pivot low higher than the previous confirmed pivot low
divergence_types.oscillator_condition: oscillator value at the new pivot is lower than at the previous pivot
quality_filters: primarily used as a continuation signal / conflict flag against an opposing change-of-character rather than scored as an independent reversal trigger
divergence_types.strength_score_hint: not scored toward reversal; used to penalize a conflicting trend_break signal in the opposite direction

divergence_types.name: hidden_bearish
divergence_types.price_condition: new confirmed pivot high lower than the previous confirmed pivot high
divergence_types.oscillator_condition: oscillator value at the new pivot is higher than at the previous pivot
quality_filters: same continuation/conflict-flag role as hidden_bullish, mirrored
divergence_types.strength_score_hint: not scored toward reversal; used to penalize a conflicting trend_break signal in the opposite direction

pseudo_code: on a confirmed price pivot low at bar B with price P: if a previous pivot low exists, compute gap_bars and price_change_pct

if gap_bars within [min_bars, max_bars] and price_change_pct >= min_price_change_pct: compare P and oscillator(B) to the previous pivot's price and oscillator value to classify regular_bullish vs hidden_bullish
mirror the same logic for confirmed price pivot highs to classify regular_bearish vs hidden_bearish
store each new pivot's bar/price/RSI/MACD-hist as the new comparison baseline
OBV divergence is computed the same way but only ever contributes as an auxiliary confluence flag, never as a primary trigger, because OBV is unbounded and has no reliable zone-based quality filter

modules.name: TrendModule
modules.responsibility: Provide a lightweight higher-timeframe directional bias as context, independent of the lower-timeframe structure engine.
inputs: HTF close via multi-timeframe data request

modules.name: StructureModule
modules.responsibility: Detect swing highs/lows, classify HH/HL/LH/LL, track confirmed trend state, and detect change-of-character (trend_break trigger) and break-of-structure (continuation context), with optional hold-bar confirmation to reduce false breakouts.

modules.name: CandlestickModule
modules.responsibility: Detect confirming/reversal candlestick patterns and score them by pattern strength, level proximity, and volume.

modules.name: DivergenceModule
modules.responsibility: Detect regular and hidden RSI/MACD-histogram divergence anchored to confirmed price pivots, and score regular divergences while flagging hidden divergences as conflict signals.

modules.name: SignalScoringModule
modules.responsibility: Combine structure, candlestick, divergence, and HTF-bias outputs into a weighted score per direction, apply mode-dependent thresholds, and emit the final classification.
inputs: confirmation-window length so component scores survive to the change-of-character bar

signal_model.scoring_model: score_direction = structure_base_score + candle_score*w_candle + divergence_score*w_divergence - hidden_conflict_penalty + htf_alignment*w_htf; a trend_break signal requires both a structure change-of-character trigger AND score_direction >= mode_threshold; component scores are held active for a configurable confirmation window (not reset every bar) so they can still contribute once the change-of-character bar arrives.

pine_script_requirements: input.* for all tunable parameters (pivot bars, ATR multiples, weights, thresholds, HTF timeframes, mode selector)
ta.pivothigh/ta.pivotlow (or equivalent) for swing detection with inherent, disclosed confirmation lag

request.security with lookahead=barmerge.lookahead_off for HTF context; any oscillator/EMA computed on the HTF series must be computed inside the request.security expression itself, not on the raw fetched series afterward, to avoid distorting the effective smoothing length
tuple destructuring for multi-value user-defined functions ([a,b,c] = f(...))
var-scoped persistent state inside user-defined functions for stateful modules (structure/hold-bar confirmation, divergence pivot tracking)
plotshape/label for signal markers, alertcondition for alerts, table.* for an on-chart score/state panel
hidden data-window plots (display.data_window) exposing raw feature/score series for dataset export
anti_repaint_notes: Pivot confirmation lag (pivot_right bars) is disclosed latency inherent to any swing-based method, not repaint — a plotted pivot never moves once printed.
The final trend_break signal is computed only from confirmed bar-close values and already-confirmed pivots/scores — no negative-offset or centered-window lookups are used.
HTF context values can change intrabar until the HTF bar itself closes — standard multi-timeframe behavior, not a repaint of already-plotted signals.
Hold-bar confirmation delays when a signal is plotted but is strictly backward-looking (only reads already-known bar indices) — it never revises a signal already drawn on a historical bar.

An opposing raw trigger arriving while a hold-bar confirmation is pending is treated as an explicit cancellation-and-restart, not a silent drop, to avoid a state-machine race that could otherwise produce an inconsistent signal history.
qa_checks: Verify HTF EMA (or any HTF oscillator) is computed inside the request.security() call, not on a locally re-smoothed staircase of already-fetched HTF values.

Verify the confirmed trend_state used to gate change-of-character/break-of-structure detection cannot be altered by a same-bar raw HH/HL/LH/LL reclassification while a hold-bar confirmation is pending.

Verify candlestick/divergence component scores are held active for a defined confirmation window rather than resetting to zero on every bar that doesn't fire a pattern, since a divergence pivot and a structure break rarely land on the exact same bar.

Verify higher-timeframe inputs are meaningfully above the chart's own timeframe (auto-scaled or explicitly validated), rather than silently defaulting to a fixed timeframe that stops being 'higher' once the chart itself is opened on 15m or 1h.

Compile in the actual Pine Editor to confirm simple-int parameter passing through user-defined functions into pivot/security calls, and confirm tuple-destructuring / line-continuation syntax, before relying on the script.

Backtest with realistic fees/slippage, check explicitly for lookahead bias, overfitting to the backtest sample, and low trade-count statistical noise before treating any performance number as validation.

notes: Outcome/label definition (e.g. forward N-bar return, max favorable/adverse excursion, or manually reviewed trend-break confirmation) belongs to the ML pipeline, not the indicator itself — the indicator only exposes confirmed, timestamped feature/score series.
True change-of-character events are rare relative to neutral bars, so expect significant class imbalance in any trend_break label; stratified sampling or class weighting is likely necessary.

Forward-return-based outcome labels should account for realistic execution assumptions (fees, slippage, achievable fill price) rather than raw close-to-close return, or the label will overstate what a strategy could actually capture.

Feature values used to build a label must be limited to information available at or before the labeled bar's close, to avoid label leakage from the same lookahead-avoidance discipline the indicator itself follows.
Volatility regime can be operationalized as an ATR percentile or realized-volatility bucket relative to a rolling lookback window, since crypto volatility is not stationary across sessions.

False-breakout labels require a short forward-looking confirmation window (e.g. does price close back through the level within M bars) and must be computed only once that window has actually elapsed, to remain leakage-free at labeling time.

overfitting_risks: Mode thresholds (strict/balanced/aggressive) and component weights are initial estimates, not calibrated against historical data — tuning them on the same sample later used to report performance would be in-sample overfitting.
Low trade/event count on 1h in particular makes any performance statistic (win rate, Sharpe-like ratios) highly sensitive to noise unless a sufficiently long and diverse sample is used.

Geometric chart-pattern heuristics (Bulkowski-style) and climax-volume thresholds are inherently loosely defined and especially prone to being tuned to fit a specific backtest window rather than generalizing.
repaint_risks: None identified as true repaint (a plotted historical signal changing after the fact) in the current design, based on static review — this has not yet been confirmed by an actual multi-session live/replay test in the Pine Editor.
Pivot confirmation lag and hold-bar confirmation delay are disclosed latency, not repaint, but should still be clearly communicated to any user relying on the indicator for manual trading.
HTF context values can shift intrabar until the higher-timeframe bar closes — normal multi-timeframe behavior, but could be mistaken for repaint if not understood.
crypto_noise_risks: Thin liquidity on altcoin pairs can produce swing points and breakouts that don't reflect genuine structural shifts, inflating false-breakout and false-signal rates relative to BTC/ETH.
Funding-rate-driven wicks on perpetual futures can trigger false-breakout or pin-bar detections unrelated to classical price-action causes.
Fragmented liquidity across exchanges means the same nominal price level can behave differently depending on the data source used.
Non-stationary volatility (session-dependent, weekend thinning) means a single fixed ATR-multiple noise filter may not generalize across time or across symbols without periodic recalibration.
implementation_limits: The current Pine Script implementation has not yet been compiled in the TradingView Pine Editor; syntax risk remains around simple-int parameter passing into pivot/security functions and tuple-destructuring line continuation.
Retest and false-breakout handling is simplified to a single hold-bar confirmation window rather than a full wick-tracking, multi-stage retest state machine.
OBV divergence and Bulkowski-style geometric chart patterns are documented as heuristic filters only and are not implemented as scored detectors in the current codebase.
The candlestick/divergence confirmation window is a fixed bar count rather than an adaptive one, and has not yet been calibrated against real data.

execution_plan.step_1: Compile the Pine Script v6 indicator in the TradingView Pine Editor and resolve any syntax errors, with particular attention to simple-int parameters passed into pivot/security calls and tuple-destructuring line continuations.
execution_plan.step_2: Run manual/visual QA on live and historical charts across 5m/15m/1h for multiple crypto pairs (at minimum BTC and one lower-liquidity altcoin) to sanity-check signal frequency and obvious false positives.
execution_plan.step_3: Run a quantitative backtest with realistic fees and slippage across all three signal modes, explicitly checking for lookahead bias, survivorship bias, and overfitting, and reporting metrics with sample-size and in-sample/out-of-sample caveats attached.
execution_plan.step_4: Build the dataset export pipeline that pulls the indicator's exposed feature/score series and applies the label definitions in ml_dataset_blueprint under a leakage-free labeling discipline.
execution_plan.step_5: Calibrate thresholds, weights, and confirmation-window length via walk-forward validation on the labeled dataset before relying on the indicator for either live manual trading or as a trusted labeling source for model training.

output_rules.if_information_is_missing: use null or empty arrays, never invent facts
